question: A circular park having a radius of 14 m. If a 1.5 m wide path is built around it, what is the approximate area of the path?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a circular path = **π × w × (2r + w)**, where **r** is the inner radius and **w** is the path width.

Given: **r** = 14 m and **w** = 1.5 m.

Area = 22/7 × 1.5 × (2 × 14 + 1.5) = 22/7 × 1.5 × 29.5

Area = 3.1415 × 1.5 × 29.5 ≈ 139.01 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 139 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Inner radius** (r) of the park = 14 m

**Width** of the path built around it = 1.5 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b239200bb4d364ae7d4f58f93697e7b3fefb4b9cf421fde25033a050611e838c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Area of Path** = Area of Outer Circle − Area of Inner Circle = πR² − πr²

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Outer radius** (R) = Inner radius + Width = 14 + 1.5 = 15.5 m

⇒ **Area of the path** = π × (R² − r²)

⇒ Area = 22/7 × (15.5² − 14²)

⇒ Area = 22/7 × (240.25 − 196)

⇒ Area = 22/7 × 44.25

⇒ Area = 973.5 ÷ 7 ≈ 139.07 m²

Rounding to the nearest whole number, we get the **approximate area** as 139 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 139 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Circle

The total space occupied by a circle is given by the formula Area = πr².

Circumference of a Circle

The boundary length of a circle is calculated as C = 2πr.

Circular Ring (Annulus)

The area between two concentric circles is Area = π(R² − r²), where R is the outer radius and r is the inner radius.
